articles.title: Listening Before Coding: Enterprise Website Discovery
articles.excerpt: How purposeful discovery conversations become specific, testable requirements for enterprise smart websites.
articles.content:
A professional photograph introduces a person; it does not prove a particular client relationship. My approach to discussing intelligent enterprise websites begins with listening. A company may initially request a redesigned homepage while its real operational problem concerns supplier access, delayed approvals or unreliable customer information. The first engagement should identify users, responsibilities and consequences of failure before choosing an application framework.

Begin with interviews that include several roles: executive sponsors, front-line operators, support staff and data owners. Ask them to describe a task as they perform it. Record the source of each observation, avoid collecting confidential records without permission and separate reported preferences from demonstrated problems. Map the current workflow and document delays, duplicate entries and decisions that have no clear owner.

Translate findings into acceptance criteria. Instead of build a smart customer portal, specify that an authenticated supplier can submit a request, receive an auditable acknowledgement and correct a failed attachment without exposing another account's records. Define authorization boundaries, expected response times, incomplete-data behavior and recovery from a disconnected external system. These conditions can be independently tested.

A first prototype should support one complete journey using authorized or synthetic data. Test an error state, denied access, mobile use and one realistic concurrency problem. Keep an architecture decision record explaining why the design is appropriate and what alternatives were considered. Passing a demonstration does not establish production readiness, but it offers concrete evidence for deciding the next step.

I welcome exploratory conversations with Vancouver organizations about such discovery-led collaborations. The image is an editorial personal portrait; it is not evidence of Canadian residency, a local business office or an established enterprise engagement. A useful outcome would be one shared problem statement and a bounded feasibility plan.

articles.title: From Livestock Field Evidence to Intelligent Economic Web Tools
articles.excerpt: What agricultural operations teach web engineers about units, provenance, scenarios and practical decisions.
articles.content:
The accompanying owner-provided collage shows an agricultural and livestock environment. It provides context for discussing the relationship between physical production and digital analysis, not documented results of a particular research study. Agricultural enterprises operate under changing feed prices, uncertain yields, biological constraints and limited managerial time. A useful web application must understand these realities instead of displaying attractive but disconnected charts.

Start with a reliable definition of the production unit. An animal group, feeding period and output measure must correspond before calculating feed conversion or enterprise margins. Record observation timestamps, units and who entered the data. Treat a missing weight, estimated consumption or changed herd composition as an explicit data-quality condition. A dashboard should never silently turn unknown observations into zeros.

Economic decision support can compare gross margin under alternative feed prices, output prices or management scenarios. Revenue, variable cost, fixed cost and working capital should remain conceptually separate. A scenario chart does not prove that an intervention will increase profit. It helps a manager understand sensitivity when the source values and assumptions are inspectable. Every illustrated farm dataset must be labeled hypothetical unless authorized field evidence supports it.

Web architecture should reflect field realities. Mobile interfaces may need low-bandwidth operation, delayed synchronization and simple forms for technicians. Managers need reviewed summaries and access-control separation from raw personal or commercial information. If external sensors or equipment are involved, use approved read-only data pathways during prototyping and seek qualified operational safety review before connecting to any physical control system.

I am interested in collaborating with agricultural technology and intelligent website teams, including potential Vancouver partners, on reproducible decision-support tools. A sensible pilot would use a synthetic livestock dataset, independently checked calculations and a small accessible interface. The picture does not establish a specific farm contract or a completed software deployment.
